Credits

The paintings, photos, models, software and fonts that PicturaAI is built from, with their sources and licences.

Paintings

All fourteen paintings are in the public domain in both the United States and the European Union: each artist died before 1956, and each work was published or exhibited before 1931. Photographs and scans of them add no new copyright. Every image comes from Wikimedia Commons and was resized and re-encoded for the web. The full reasoning for each work is in the presets notes on GitHub.

  • The Starry Night. Vincent van Gogh, The Starry Night, 1889. Museum of Modern Art, New York. Source file for The Starry Night. Licence: Public domain.
  • The Scream. Edvard Munch, The Scream, 1893. National Museum, Oslo. Source file for The Scream. Licence: Public domain.
  • The Great Wave off Kanagawa. Katsushika Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa, c. 1831. Modern recut impression, c. 1930. Source file for The Great Wave off Kanagawa. Licence: Public domain.
  • The Wreck of a Transport Ship. J. M. W. Turner, The Wreck of a Transport Ship, c. 1810. Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, Lisbon. Museum photograph by Benoît Prieur, who released it as CC0. Source file for The Wreck of a Transport Ship. Licence: Public domain.
  • Udnie (Young American Girl, The Dance). Francis Picabia, Udnie (Young American Girl, The Dance), 1913. Centre Pompidou, Paris. Source file for Udnie (Young American Girl, The Dance). Licence: Public domain.
  • Improvisation 27 (Garden of Love II). Wassily Kandinsky, Improvisation 27 (Garden of Love II), 1912. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Mount margins cropped. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases the image as CC0 Open Access. Source file for Improvisation 27 (Garden of Love II). Licence: CC0.
  • The Large Blue Horses. Franz Marc, The Large Blue Horses, 1911. Walker Art Center, Minneapolis. Source file for The Large Blue Horses. Licence: Public domain.
  • The Kiss. Gustav Klimt, The Kiss, 1907–1908. Belvedere, Vienna. Source file for The Kiss. Licence: Public domain.
  • A Sunday on La Grande Jatte. Georges Seurat, A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884–1886. Art Institute of Chicago. Source file for A Sunday on La Grande Jatte. Licence: Public domain.
  • Woman with a Hat. Henri Matisse, Woman with a Hat, 1905. San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. Source file for Woman with a Hat. Licence: Public domain.
  • Café Terrace at Night. Vincent van Gogh, Café Terrace at Night, 1888. Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo. Source file for Café Terrace at Night. Licence: Public domain.
  • Zodiac. Alphonse Mucha, Zodiac, 1896. Colour lithograph. Paper margins cropped. The Commons file name says 1869 by mistake; the work dates from 1896. Source file for Zodiac. Licence: Public domain.
  • Sloop, Nassau. Winslow Homer, Sloop, Nassau, 1899. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Source file for Sloop, Nassau. Licence: Public domain.
  • Splashed-Ink Landscape. Sesshū Tōyō, Splashed-Ink Landscape, 1495. Tokyo National Museum. Source file for Splashed-Ink Landscape. Licence: Public domain.

Sample photos

The three photos under “Try a sample” are released under CC0, so they need no credit. We credit them anyway.

  • Golden Retriever in a forest. Photo by Johan Spaedtke. Source file for Golden Retriever in a forest. Licence: CC0.
  • Herzog-Friedrich-Strasse in the old town of Innsbruck, Austria. Photo by Wilfredor. Source file for Herzog-Friedrich-Strasse in the old town of Innsbruck, Austria. Licence: CC0.
  • Clouds mirrored in Lake Bohinj, Slovenia. Photo by Ales Krivec. Source file for Clouds mirrored in Lake Bohinj, Slovenia. Licence: CC0.

Models and software

  • Arbitrary Image Stylization v1-256, Google Magenta. The style transfer model, used both on the server and, converted to TensorFlow.js, in your browser. Ghiasi, Lee, Kudlur, Dumoulin and Shlens, “Exploring the structure of a real-time, arbitrary neural artistic stylization network”, BMVC 2017. Licence: Apache License 2.0.
  • DeepLab-v3 (MediaPipe Image Segmenter model), Google. Finds the subject for “Style the subject” and “Style the background”, on your device. Licence: Apache License 2.0.
  • TensorFlow.js 4.22.0, Google. Runs the model in the browser. Licence: Apache License 2.0.
  • MediaPipe Tasks Vision 0.10.35, Google. Runs the segmentation model. Loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net. Licence: Apache License 2.0.
  • TensorFlow, Google. Runs the model on the server. Licence: Apache License 2.0.
  • FastAPI, Sebastián Ramírez. The web server. Licence: MIT License.
  • Pillow, Jeffrey A. Clark and contributors. Reads, checks and writes images on the server. Licence: MIT-CMU License.
  • NumPy, The NumPy developers. Image maths on the server. Licence: BSD 3-Clause License.

Fonts

  • Libre Caslon Display by Pablo Impallari. Titles and painting names. Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Served by Google Fonts.
  • Schibsted Grotesk by Bakken & Bæck for Schibsted. Everything else. Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Served by Google Fonts.

PicturaAI itself

The PicturaAI code is open source under the MIT License. It is on GitHub.

Paintings you upload under “Your painting” are not part of the collection and are not kept. Only use paintings you have the right to use; see the terms.
